summary: Deployment configuration is well-structured. Services are correctly isolated from Universal Paywall. Healthchecks and startup ordering are correct. Required fixes: (1) no .gitignore — secrets risk, (2) nginx Content-Type add_header breaks SSE streaming, (3) client_max_body_size not set — 1MB nginx default will block large memory captures. Minor improvements: rate limiting, server_tokens, image pinning.

findings.title: Missing client_max_body_size — nginx default 1MB blocks 10MB memory_capture
findings.description: nginx's default `client_max_body_size` is 1MB. The application-level limit (D8) is 10MB for memory_capture content. Without overriding this, a PDF file >1MB sent to memory_capture will be rejected by nginx with a 413 Request Entity Too Large HTML error — not a JSON error from memory-hub. This breaks the D8 content limit entirely at the nginx level.
findings.recommendation:
Add inside the HTTPS server block:
```nginx
client_max_body_size 11m;
```
This allows up to 11MB request bodies, letting memory-hub's own 10MB limit apply and return a proper JSON error.

findings.title: Content-Type: application/json at server level will break SSE streaming
findings.description: MCP's Streamable HTTP transport uses SSE (text/event-stream) for streaming responses. Adding `add_header Content-Type 'application/json' always` at the server level overrides the upstream Content-Type header for ALL responses. This will corrupt MCP streaming sessions where the client expects text/event-stream.
findings.recommendation: Remove line 117. The Content-Type for 401 errors from `return 401 '...'` will be text/plain by default, which is acceptable. Upstream proxied responses will correctly carry their original Content-Type (application/json for RPC, text/event-stream for SSE).

findings.title: No .gitignore — MNEMONIC_IDENTITY (Ed25519 private key) and MEMORY_API_KEY risk git exposure
findings.description: No .gitignore exists. .env containing MNEMONIC_IDENTITY, MNEMONIC_JWT, and MEMORY_API_KEY can be accidentally committed.
findings.recommendation: Create .gitignore with .env, node_modules/, etc. (See SA7-1 for full content.)

findings.title: Dockerfile image not pinned to digest — oven/bun:1.3.10-slim tag is mutable
findings.description: Docker image tags are mutable — `oven/bun:1.3.10-slim` could be republished with a different underlying OS image. For production deployments, pinning to a specific digest ensures reproducibility.
findings.recommendation:
Pin to digest for production:
```dockerfile
FROM oven/bun:1.3.10-slim@sha256:<digest>
```
Or at minimum document that the tag should be verified: `docker pull oven/bun:1.3.10-slim && docker inspect oven/bun:1.3.10-slim --format='{{.Id}}'`

findings.title: No rate limiting — risk of DoS and resource exhaustion
findings.description: No limit_req_zone directive. memory_think LLM calls can take 2-10s and are expensive. Without rate limiting, a client (or attacker with the token) can submit unbounded concurrent memory_think requests, potentially exhausting Postgres connections and memory.
findings.recommendation: See SA7-3 for rate limiting nginx config. Recommend limiting to 30r/m (generous for single-user) with burst=10.

findings.title: No resource limits on memory-hub or postgres containers
findings.description: docker-compose.yml doesn't set `mem_limit` or `cpus`. A runaway LLM synthesis call or large PDF ingestion could exhaust host memory, impacting other VPS services.
findings.recommendation:
Add resource limits to both services:
```yaml
memory-hub:
  deploy:
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: 2g
        cpus: '2.0'

postgres:
  deploy:
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: 1g
        cpus: '1.0'
```

findings.title: server_tokens not disabled — nginx version exposed
findings.recommendation: Add `server_tokens off;` to the HTTPS server block.

findings.title: DATABASE_URL :? without message text gives unhelpful startup error
findings.description: Line 54: `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?}` — no error message. Compare with line 24's `:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required`. Inconsistency.

findings.title: Service isolation is correct — memory-hub can be started independently
findings.description: `docker compose up memory-hub postgres -d` starts only these two services. No shared network or volume references to Universal Paywall services. `docker compose up memory-hub -d --no-deps` also works correctly. The acceptance criterion 'does NOT restart paywall services' is met.

findings.title: Healthcheck with condition: service_healthy correctly gates memory-hub on Postgres
findings.description: memory-hub waits for postgres to pass its pg_isready healthcheck before starting. This prevents the gbrain Postgres engine from attempting to connect during DB initialization, avoiding connection errors on cold start.

findings.title: Dockerfile workspace path layout mirrors repo — bun workspace resolution correct
findings.description: The Dockerfile sets up /app/packages/memory-hub/ and /app/vendors/gbrain/, mirroring the repo's relative path structure. bun.lock's workspace reference `../../vendors/gbrain` resolves correctly to /app/vendors/gbrain from /app/packages/memory-hub/. Layer ordering (manifest COPYs before source COPYs) enables correct Docker layer caching.
